verdict.rationale: Conta Simples' own API lets a server-to-server integration access card and bank statements and update and reconcile transactions. It also manages categories, cost centers and suppliers used to classify expenses, so an agent can pull transactions and write coding back. The evidence does not show a way to fetch only uncoded transactions, any policy-flag fields, or a review stage for agent-written coding; updates appear to apply directly. Missing for 10: MCP server, uncoded-transaction filter, policy flag support, review/approval queue for pushed coding, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can pull uncoded transactions via API or MCP, propose categorizations and policy flags, and push clean coding back for review

citations.quote: Access card and bank statements, download receipts, update and reconcile transactions.
List, create, rename, and delete categories to classify transactions.
List, create, rename, and delete cost centers to classify company expenses.
The Conta Simples API uses OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials for authentication. This flow is suited for server-to-server calls without an end user.
